name: Lazarus NB-4 'Jellyfish'
description:
A launcher that fires a 2-meter conductive mesh net that wraps around the target and delivers a sustained electrical discharge through its entire surface area. The Jellyfish combines physical restraint with electrical incapacitation — the target is simultaneously immobilized by the weighted net and subjected to a full-body shock that prevents any coordinated muscle movement to escape. The net's conductive fibers are woven with shape-memory alloy that contracts upon deployment, tightening around the target and increasing electrical contact area.

Lazarus designed the NB-4 for live capture operations where the target must be taken intact — corporate espionage extraction, witness retrieval, and bounty collection. The Jellyfish is the preferred tool for operatives who need their target alive, conscious, and unable to resist. The net's shape-memory contraction means that struggling makes the restraint tighter and the electrical contact more complete, creating a negative feedback loop that punishes resistance until the target stops moving.

The weapon's most disturbing characteristic is its duration. The net's integrated battery sustains the electrical discharge for up to three minutes — far longer than necessary for incapacitation. Lazarus claims the extended duration is a safety feature that ensures the target remains incapacitated during operator approach. Critics note that three minutes of full-body electrical discharge causes lasting nerve damage and psychological trauma that serves no legitimate operational purpose.
specifications: range: 8 meters net diameter: 2 meters deployed discharge: 30,000 volts sustained, 3-minute battery net weight: 1.2 kg launcher weight: 2.1 kg length: 340mm reload: Single-use net cartridge
tactical_use: Live capture and restraint. Operators fire the Jellyfish at targets who must be taken alive, then approach once the electrical discharge has ensured compliance. The net can be deactivated manually by the operator or will exhaust its battery after three minutes. Effective against augmented targets — the full-body discharge affects biological and cybernetic systems simultaneously.
cultural_context: The Jellyfish has become associated with forced extraction and kidnapping. Being 'jellied' is slang for being captured against your will, and the weapon's distinctive deployment sound — a wet snap as the net expands — is recognized and feared in communities where extraction operations are common. Bounty hunters who carry Jellyfish launchers are treated with particular wariness.
known_users: Known to be used by criminal kidnapping operations
story_hooks: A Jellyfish net has been recovered from a crime scene with modifications — the electrical discharge has been replaced with a chemical payload that absorbs through the skin on contact. Someone is converting restraint tools into poison delivery systems.

A bounty hunter's Jellyfish launcher has been traced to three separate abductions — but the bounty hunter died six months ago. Someone is using a dead operator's equipment and license to conduct extractions under a ghost identity.
related_entities: Arcturus Defense Solutions CrisisNet BT-4 Battlefield Triage

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, predatory launcher with an organic aesthetic that evokes its namesake. The barrel splays slightly at the muzzle like tentacle openings, with a bulbous capacitor chamber dominating the rear section. The overall silhouette is aggressive yet ergonomic — something designed to be gripped firmly and aimed with deliberation.
physical_description.dimensions: 340mm length, 120mm width at capacitor housing, 85mm height. Barrel spreads to 110mm at muzzle aperture.
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively dense — feels heavier than its 2.1kg suggests due to concentrated mass in the capacitor. Balanced slightly forward toward the barrel, requiring a firm two-handed grip or a single reinforced grip on trained operators.
physical_description.primary_material: Titanium-reinforced polymer frame with integrated heatsinks. Capacitor housing is brushed steel with embedded cooling fins.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal polymer body with high-gloss gunmetal accents around the trigger assembly and muzzle. Cooling fins on the capacitor have a satin nickel finish that catches light when discharged.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep charcoal gray primary with electric blue accent striping along the barrel ridges and capacitor vents. Trigger housing is flat black.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer with aggressive diamond-pattern knurling for wet or augmented-hand operation. Slightly tacky, heat-resistant elastomer coating.
distinctive_features: Splayed muzzle aperture resembles jellyfish tentacle roots
Three parallel cooling fins running the length of the capacitor housing, pulsing with faint bioluminescent charge indicators
LED status ring around the trigger guard — cycles blue (armed), amber (discharging), red (depleted)
Etched charge count window on the left side showing cartridge remaining
Faint electrical scorch marks around the muzzle from deployment stress
Small vent ports along the barrel that emit faint ozone smell when active
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: LAZARUS BIOWORKS logo embossed on the left side of the capacitor housing in matte black. Serial number stamped into the grip. Tier-3 licensing plate recessed into the right side frame.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained but showing field wear. Light polymer scuffs from equipment racks, faint electrical burn marks around the muzzle aperture from repeated deployment. Capacitor fins may show dust accumulation or slight discoloration from sustained-discharge residue.
